newsitem.title: USA: Powerful storm knocks out power in Sierra Nevada.
newsitem.headline: Powerful storm knocks out power in Sierra Nevada.

text.p: A powerful storm blanketed the Sierra Nevada with snow and freezing rain on Sunday, knocking out power to tens of thousands of homes and closing some mountain highways.
About 40,000 Pacific Gas & Electric Co. customers in the Sierra foothills were without power due to the heavy snowfall, PG&E spokesman Leonard Anderson said.
"The whole Sierra's getting pummeled," Anderson said, adding that it could take until Christmas Eve to restore power to affected customers.
Along the northern California coast, gusting winds knocked down poles and power lines, causing scattered power outages and wreaking havoc for last-minute holiday shoppers and travelers.
Mudslides and airport tie-ups were reported in the San Francisco Bay area. A tornado touched down in the wine country, destroying two outbuildings, Napa County officials said.

Since Friday, the blustery storm has affected nearly 100,000 PG&E customers, Anderson said. So far, it has dumped up to eight feet of snow in the Lake Tahoe area on the northern California-Nevada border, according to the National Weather Service.
The heavy snow closed some highways through the mountains between California and Nevada, the California Highway Patrol said. Authorities urged people to make only necessary trips.

"The roads are blocked by low visibility and by people skidding into snow banks," said Highway Patrol dispatcher Gina Moran in Truckee, Calif., about 30 miles west of Reno, Nevada. "It has been a pretty ugly sight."
Forecasters said weather from San Francisco to the Sierra should improve.
